intro: Five threads worth watching across drug development this week — a clear point of view, with the sources to back it. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: Protein degraders have moved from promise to big-pharma balance sheets
narratives.detail: Roche put $700M down (up to $2.3B) for Nurix's BTK-degrader, and optioned immunology and neurology alongside it — the second large-cap degrader deal this window. The signal is hard to miss: this is now a Phase 3-stage commercial platform, not an early-stage bet.

narratives.headline: KRAS is now a three-class target
narratives.detail: J&J paid $1B in cash for preclinical Firefly Bio, pricing a KRAS-targeting ADC before a single patient is dosed. Covalent inhibitors, RAS(ON) agents, and now ADCs are all chasing the same target everyone spent a decade calling undruggable.

narratives.headline: The incretin tolerability ceiling is real at Phase 3 scale
narratives.detail: Survodutide posted ~19% discontinuations in SYNCHRONIZE-1 — roughly 2.5–5× the Phase 2 class baseline. The GLP-1/glucagon tolerability ceiling is now a live constraint on retatrutide and CagriSema, not a footnote.

narratives.headline: Obesity's next contest is the triple-agonist class
narratives.detail: Novo's 2030 triple-agonist commitment turns this into a two-sponsor race against Lilly's retatrutide. The open question is whether the Phase 3 weight-loss ceiling actually moves, or whether tolerability eats the gains.

narratives.headline: M&A heat is sustained at the top end — even in a 'quiet' month
narratives.detail: Seven multibillion-dollar takeouts closed in a month trade press called quiet. By deal count it looks slow; weighted by value, the top end is clearly still active — and it's holding across oncology, hepatology and rare disease. Deal-value is the signal to watch, not deal-count.
